# 1 Samuel Chapter 31 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 168r–168v | **Source Image:** 1SA_031_page_001.jpg, 1SA_031_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The Philistines attacked Israel, and the Israelites fled before them. Many fell dead on Mount Gilboa.

**2** The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua — Saul's sons.

**3** The fighting grew fierce around Saul. The archers found him, and he was critically wounded.

**4** Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, before these uncircumcised men come and run me through and abuse my body." But the armor-bearer was terrified and refused. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

**5** When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died alongside him.

**6** So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that day.

**7** When the Israelites on the other side of the valley and across the Jordan saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and ran. The Philistines came and occupied them.

**8** The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

**9** They cut off Saul's head and stripped off his armor. Then they sent messengers throughout Philistine territory to spread the news in the temples of their idols and among the people.

**10** They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

**11** When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,

**12** all their bravest men set out and marched through the night. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and cremated them there.

**13** Then they took the bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **31:2 — Jonathan**: The most heartbreaking casualty. Jonathan — David's beloved friend, the man who renounced his own claim to the throne — dies beside the father he loved despite everything. The text gives no speech, no final scene. Just his name in a list of the dead.

2. **31:4 — "abuse my body"**: The Hebrew hit'alelu means "make sport of, mock." Saul's final fear is not death but humiliation — the same concern that drove his entire reign. Even at the end, his identity crisis defines him.

3. **31:9 — "good news"**: The Hebrew root b-s-r — the same root that will become "gospel" — is used for the Philistine victory announcement. Their good news is Israel's catastrophe. The word will be reclaimed in 2 Samuel 1.

4. **31:11-13 — Jabesh-gilead's final loyalty**: The book ends where Saul's story began. In chapter 11, his first act as king was rescuing Jabesh-gilead from mutilation. Now the men of Jabesh-gilead repay that debt — marching all night through enemy territory to rescue his mutilated body. It is an act of extraordinary courage and loyalty, and it gives Saul's tragic story its one note of grace.

5. **31:13 — the tamarisk tree**: Saul once sat under a tamarisk tree, holding court as king (22:6). Now he is buried beneath one. The tree of his authority becomes the marker of his grave. The book of 1 Samuel is over.

— PNEUMA
